corrected_attribution: Every historical "file_scope": null line traces to exactly one commit: c1e5f5c3d (2026-07-27, "specs: repair stale Theories/Bimodal path references after library rename"), a one-off manual/agent path-reference repair that rewrote file_scope arrays and, in doing so, introduced literal nulls on tasks whose arrays were emptied. These were removed by 3f4599425 (2026-10-03, "specs: drop literal-null file_scope keys on five never-planned tasks"). The three archival/orchestration commits previously blamed (81647f25c, cb74c4c67, b12283595) never introduced a null -- git log -S matches any change to the pickaxe string's occurrence COUNT, and these commits appear in that search only because they REMOVED pre-existing nulls (via archiving the affected tasks out of active_projects), not because they wrote one. No current script constructs a file_scope: null write; the only occurrences of the literal string in the source store are test fixtures (test-orchestrate-predispatch-review.sh, test-backfill-file-scope.sh, test-orchestrate-build-dispatch.sh, test-orchestrate-batch-admit.sh, test-validate-state.sh) and one worked example in context/contracts/territory.md. Item 1 closes as a no-op: there is no live writer to fix.
